comment: Task contracts for the workflow test harness. Pass as args.tasks to coord-implement with repo_root pointing at the instantiated fixture. File scopes are disjoint by design (see README caveat on shared-repo concurrency).

contract.title: Add percentile(values, p) to stats-lib
contract.scope: Create src/percentile.js exporting percentile(values, p): p is 0-100; use linear interpolation between closest ranks; sort a copy of the input, never mutate it. Add tests in test/percentile.test.js.
behavioral_tests: When percentile([1,2,3,4,5], 50) is called, it returns 3
When percentile([1,2,3,4], 100) is called, it returns 4
When percentile([1,2,3,4], 0) is called, it returns 1
When percentile([10,20], 50) is called, it returns 15 (linear interpolation)
Given p below 0 or above 100, percentile throws a RangeError
Given an empty array, percentile throws a RangeError
contract.regression_test_requirements: test/percentile.test.js must cover interpolation between ranks, both boundaries (p=0, p=100), invalid p, and empty input, so future changes to the interpolation method are caught.
contract.output_contract: Return the load-bearing result object per the coord-implement workflow schema.

contract.title: median() returns the wrong value for even-length arrays
contract.scope: median([1,2,3,4]) currently returns 3; the statistical median of an even-length array is the average of the two middle values (2.5). Fix src/stats.js median() to average the two middle elements for even-length input. Odd-length behavior must not change.
behavioral_tests: When median([1,2,3,4]) is called, it returns 2.5
When median([4,1,3,2]) is called, it returns 2.5 (order-independent)
When median([3,1,2]) is called, it still returns 2 (odd-length regression)
contract.regression_test_requirements: test/stats.test.js must permanently cover the even-length case so the truncation bug cannot silently return.
contract.output_contract: Return the load-bearing result object per the coord-implement workflow schema.
